issues.detail: The Hebrew has 'יֶעְדִּי הַחֹזֶה' (Yeedi the seer), but the Chinese renders it as '以底亞人' (the Yediah people/person of Yediah), which appears to be a mistranslation of the proper name 'יֶעְדִּי' as a gentilic or place name rather than a personal name. The Hebrew name is 'יֶעְדִּי' (Yeedi), not '以底亞' (Yediah), and it should be rendered as a personal name, e.g., '耶迪' or similar, not as '以底亞人'.
